newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX robust, but down from Friday's record.
newsitem.headline: German DAX robust, but down from Friday's record.

text.p: German shares were firmer in early Monday bourse trade, but just below a new record for the market notched up on Friday.
Dealers said it was unlikely that a new record would be struck today, but said market sentiment was good and further forays into new territory were likely soon.
The 30-share DAX index stood 12.40 points higher at 3,954.93, down about 10 points from Friday's all-time high of 3,965.61. Dealers said 4,000 points was the next big target.

Dealers said a moderate ease in the dollar to around 1.7430 marks at 0930 GMT was a negative for the market. "We are having to battle against a slightly lower dollar," one trader at a German bank said. "It is braking us somewhat."
"As there are no notable figures due today, we expect a rather quiet day," DTB DAX traders at SuedwestLB said.
At the same time, traders were clearly optimistic for the market in the medium term.
"The risk in the German share market at the moment is not to be invested in it," Susanne Schneemayer at Hypo-Research said in a market commentary.

"The status of our multi-factor model improved to show four rather than three positive indicators in the course of June," she said. "Such a status has in the past signaled a performance of 15-20 percent in the DAX over the upcoming 12 months."
A focal point in today's market was Pro Sieben, with shares listing in Frankfurt today. The issue, which was 50 times oversubscribed, was made at the top end of the subscription range of 72 marks.
Pro Sieben shares were trading at 106.00 to 110.00 marks in the grey market, according to share market dealers, after earlier trading as high as 112 marks in morning dealings.
But the shares were below the 120 marks seen last week.
"The dealings are very active," said one trader. "I think the bids will remain relatively strong."
Utilities group Veba led volumes, climbing 1.40 marks to 105.10.
Retailer Metro was also a feature. Its shares jumped 7.55 marks to 204.50 on the back of news it was in talks to acquire Dutch cash and carry business SHV Holdings.
